recovery.momentumLow: Watch for green shoots — they count
recovery.alertText: 3+ recovery signs logged. Tell them what you see — specific, brief, no strings: "I noticed you've made every meeting this week. I see the work."

signs.label: Open about whereabouts without being asked
Showing interest in others' lives again

privacyNote: Tracking isn't surveillance — it turns anxiety into observation, and observation into a plan. Recovery signs matter as much as warning signs: they teach your eyes what healing looks like.
privacyNoteCoach: Your log is visible to you and your coach.
privacyNoteDirect: Your log is visible only to you.

window.openBody: A consequence can create a short opening — not a guarantee. Defenses often rebuild within roughly 24–72 hours. Move calmly and use what is already prepared.
window.sayText: “What happened is serious. You do not have to solve everything today. We have help ready, and we can leave now if you are willing.”
window.readinessReadyBody: Reconfirm the bed and admissions contact now, then follow the departure plan.
window.readinessBody: Do not improvise a planned conversation. Finish the concrete logistics privately — but never delay immediate voluntary help.
window.readinessUnavailable: Treatment readiness could not be opened
window.readinessUnavailableBody: Protected plan details are unavailable. Open the plan and recover access before relying on its readiness status.
window.readinessSavingBody: Wait for the protected save to finish before treating the plan as green.
window.readinessUnsaved: Treatment Action Plan is not safely saved
window.readinessUnsavedBody: Open the plan and retry the protected save. Do not treat it as green until saving is confirmed.
window.closedTitle: Did a major consequence just happen?
window.closedBody: Families often speak when they have reached their own limit. A more useful opening may follow a concrete consequence, when the person can briefly see what their use is costing them.
window.saveError: The consequence could not be saved. Nothing was changed.
window.loadErrorTitle: The consequence log could not be opened
window.loadErrorBody: Existing timing information may still be stored. Retry before logging anything new so an active window is not hidden or overwritten.
window.safety: If there is an overdose, severe withdrawal, medical danger, suicidal behavior, violence, or immediate danger, call 911 or 988 now. If they ask for treatment now, act now — do not wait for a checklist.
window.removeBody: Use this only if the event was logged by mistake. Removing it closes the current willingness window unless an earlier event is still active.

trajectory.title: Your trajectory
trajectory.subtitle: Six weeks of warning and recovery signs, side by side. Patterns are easier to read across weeks than days.
trajectory.trendWorsening: Warning signs have been climbing lately.
trajectory.trendImproving: Recovery is gaining ground — keep going.
trajectory.trendNone: Log a few weeks to see your trend here.
trajectory.selfCheckTitle: Is it time for an intervention?
trajectory.selfCheckSub: There's no right answer — just notice what feels true. Nothing happens unless you choose it.
selfCheckItems: The same problems keep coming back, even with boundaries in place.
Their use is putting someone's safety at risk.
I've tried talking with them on my own and it hasn't changed things.
I'm running out of next steps I can take alone.
Other people who love them are worried too.
trajectory.selfCheckResult: Several of these ring true. Planning ahead with a professional might help — and you don't have to decide anything today.
trajectory.shareBody: Send your coach a note so they can see how things are trending and reach out.
trajectory.shareDone: Shared — your coach will see this.
trajectory.shareLocked: Turn on coach sharing in Settings to share your trajectory.
trajectory.shareMessage: I'd like to talk about how things have been trending over the last several weeks. Can we connect?
